subject: Private cluster: HW profile, NIC split and storage evacuation plan
messages:

Cc: Eng Lead <eng-lead@graniteworks.com>

Subject: Private cluster: initial asks for NIC mapping + storage evacuation

Hi Mina,

We're lining up hardware and network for the private cluster at our Austin site and need guidance on two things before procurement:

1) NIC topology — we currently have dual NICs per server (1Gb mgmt + 25Gb data) but our ops team is asking whether a split with dedicated 10Gb management and bonded 40Gb data per server would be safer for future throughput. Any downsides for Redwood's runtime?

2) Storage evacuation — for maintenance windows we want a predictable plan to evacuate local NVMe-backed ephemeral caches and move critical PVs. Can you share an evacuation strategy that minimizes rollback risk and keeps tail latency predictable?

Also attaching our preliminary BOM (work-in-progress).

Thanks,
Mark
Operations Infrastructure
GraniteWorks

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Infrastructure <ops+infrastructure@graniteworks.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster: initial asks for NIC mapping + storage evacuation

Thanks Mark — good questions. High level answers up front, then an operational plan.

Summary recommendations:
- NIC split: prefer 1Gb (OOB) management + 25/40Gb bonded data lane. Keep an uninterrupted management path separate from your data fabric.
- Data path: use LACP bonded pair or SR-IOV for high-throughput pods; avoid mixing control plane traffic on the same bond.
- Evacuation: two-phase approach — graceful poddrain + live KV-cache shard flush, then async PV migration for critical stateful workloads. For ephemeral caches, prefer replicated warming rather than bulk rsync during maintenance.

Operational details (short):
- Topology: 1Gb out-of-band (OOB) to an isolated management switch per rack. Data NICs on top-of-rack (TOR) 25/40Gb spine — tag VLANs per tenant and reserve a dedicated egress queue for inference model fetches.
- MTU: set 9000 for data VLANs; keep mgmt VLAN at 1500. Make sure NIC drivers are pinned to stable kernel builds (we recommend the RedHat/CentOS 8.6 driver stack or Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with the vendor NIC firmware).
- Node pools: create three node pools — control-plane-light (CPU-heavy, no GPUs), inference-general (mixed CPUs + GPU types), and scratch-fast (local NVMe for ephemeral caches). Use taints/tolerations for scheduling.

Evacuation playbook (maintenance window):
1) Preflight (T-48h): snapshot cluster state (etcd backup), validate replica counts, and run a dry-run of drain on a canary node.
2) Canaries (T-24h): pick one rack node; execute: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120; observe 30m for latency spikes.
3) KV/Cache flush: for our LRU-based inference caches, call the runtime endpoint to shard-serialize in-memory KV to the warmed-replica. If warmed-replica not available, export prefix keys to objectstore (S3) with expiry.
4) Ephemeral NVMe handling: do NOT rsync full cache during a short window. Instead: promote warmed replicas and allow traffic to flow to replicas; for datasets >50GB schedule async background sync to S3 during off-peak.
5) PV migration: use rsync for non-database filesystems; for model artifacts use block-level replication (e.g., DRBD or storage vendor snapshot replication) followed by quick failover.
6) Restore: reverse the sequence, validate token latencies and cold-start error rate <0.5%.

I'll attach a draft playbook and a concise BOM mapping. Vanessa/Karthik — tagging you for procurement and network policy checks.

- Mina
Mina Haddad
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Mark — procurement note from our side:
- BOM: please include exact SKU for NICs (vendor + part) and whether you need single or dual PSUs for hot-swap policy. We prefer spares on-site (1 spare per 20 nodes) for racks hosting inference-general.
- Warranty & firmware: require extended FW support window aligned to 36 months.
- Timeline: once SKUs confirmed we can lock a delivery SLA of 6 weeks for US regions.

Operational asks: please confirm whether virtualization (VMs) will be used for control-plane testing; if so we recommend dedicating a small host-aggregate for VMs to keep hypervisor noise out of inference node pools.

I'll add procurement tasks to JIRA-RW-4821.

Subject: Re: Private cluster: HW profile, NIC split and storage evacuation plan

Thanks for the detailed plan. A couple clarifications from our infra team after reviewing the playbook: 

1) For NVMe eviction you recommend promoting warmed replicas — what would you advise for a dataset with high checksum churn where warming replicas takes hours? Is there a fallback technique that doesn't increase cold-start latency beyond 10%?

2) For bonded data NICs, do we need per-node SR-IOV configuration or will a software-bond with tuned IRQ affinity be sufficient for Redwood's serving runtime?

3) SLA during a maintenance window — can Redwood commit to a degradation window of 30 minutes per node drain for production inference (p95 latency goal)?

We'll include the SKU details and confirm whether hypervisor testbeds are used.

-Mark

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Infrastructure <ops+infrastructure@graniteworks.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster: HW profile, NIC split and storage evacuation plan

Mark — quick answers and action items: 

Bullet answers:
- High-churn datasets: introduce a two-tier strategy — quick-hot-cache (small, kept in RAM with aggressive replication) and bulk-warm (on NVMe + background sync to S3). For churny keys, replicate in-memory to at least two peers before draining. This keeps cold-start latency within ~7–9% in our internal tests.
- NIC config: SR-IOV adds determinism and we recommend SR-IOV for inference-general pools if your NICs support it. If not available, software-bond with tuned IRQ affinity + CPU pinning works but needs careful testing.
- SLA: Redwood can commit to a 30-minute soft window during planned maintenance provided the cluster follows the preflight and canary steps and has hot spares per Vanessa's BOM ratio. We'll record this as a one-off exception in the SOW for GW-PI-3892.

Action items assigned: 
- Mark (GraniteWorks): confirm SKUs and whether SR-IOV-capable NICs are in the BOM (due EOD Fri).
- Vanessa: add spare-policy to JIRA-RW-4821 and assign procurement owner.
- Mina: ITP (implementation test plan) for the canary drain — please publish a 1-page checklist in the runbook link.

I'll update the SOW draft and link the Doc here once done.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
